Ascertain

ass-er-TAIN -- three syllables, stress on the last syllable, TAIN. · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To ascertain is to learn or find out something for certain.

Investigators are still working to ascertain how the fire began.

Worked Example

Nobody at the desk can say whether the shipment left the warehouse. So the manager pulls the loading log, calls the driver, checks the gate camera for Tuesday afternoon -- and only then writes 'departed 4:15 p.m.' on the form.

The manager did not guess; he ascertained the fact. To ascertain is to learn or find out something and nail it down for certain, usually by checking rather than assuming.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

verify: To verify is to check that a fact you already have is accurate -- you recount the cash, re-run the numbers, compare the copies. To ascertain is to find the fact out in the first place. Verify tests an answer already in hand, while ascertain hunts the answer down.

confirm: To confirm is to make something you already believe official -- you expect a yes and simply collect it. Ascertain starts further back: you do not yet know the fact and must dig it out. A nod for what you suspected confirms it; it does not ascertain anything.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

assume: accept something as true without checking

speculate: guess without evidence

Where it sits · how firmly the fact is verified — determine → ascertain → establish

determine vs. ascertain: Determine is the everyday partner -- you can determine your route in ten seconds with a map -- while ascertain implies deliberate checking, the sort a careful investigator does before writing anything down.

establish vs. ascertain: Establish goes furthest: you ascertain a fact for your own certainty, but you establish it so firmly that nobody else can dispute it either.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — as-

prefix — as-: to, toward (Latin ad-)

root — certain

root — certain: sure, settled, decided (Latin certus, from cernere 'to sift, to decide')

Put it together

Put it together: Ascertain is ad- ('to') plus certain, from Latin certus, 'settled' -- itself the past participle of cernere, 'to sift.' To ascertain is to make something certain: you sift the evidence until only the settled fact is left. That is the very same cernere behind discern, this unit's other sifting word.

Use the root in a new word: certificate

Use the root in a new word: certificate: The dive shop would not rent the tanks without a certificate proving she had trained.

Root Check

Word Choice

Ascertain is a formal verb for careful fact-finding: ascertain the cause, ascertain whether the report is accurate, ascertain the extent of the damage. It always implies that you checked. If you only think something is probably true, you are assuming or estimating, not ascertaining.
